done_when: Every Forge repo's AGENTS.md tells agents to file a Forge bug with the bug template, and the template asks for everything needed to reproduce and fix it without any client code, names or secrets

known.title: Not done: Forge bug reports do not use the bug template
Not done: proof that the bug template retains required prompts
Forge bug template command fails in Windows PowerShell
Not done: test_1_clients_are_told_to_file_forge_bugs does not prove template use

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. The guide pipes the GitHub response to `base64 --decode`, but `base64` is not a standard PowerShell command. The supported Windows installer directs agents to open a PowerShell window (`scripts/install-windows.ps1:130`), so an agent following this guide there cannot fetch the template text needed to file the report.
findings.title: Forge bug template command fails in Windows PowerShell

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The test checks for `Forge bug` anywhere in AGENTS.md, but never checks the instruction to use the template. Replacing “with the Forge bug template's sections” with “as a Forge bug” would leave every assertion green while removing a named Done-when requirement.
findings.title: Not done: test_1_clients_are_told_to_file_forge_bugs does not prove template use

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The fixed `PROMPTS` list still omits the prior Forge version, whether the repo is new or adopted, and the workaround. Deleting those requests from the template and both guides would leave the named proof green, although the template currently asks for them at `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/forge-bug.md:22` and `:28` to reproduce and fix the bug.
findings.title: Not done: proof that the bug template retains required prompts

why: When a coding agent hits a Forge bug in a client repo, nothing tells it to report the bug to Forge, so the Forge team learns late and without the details needed to fix it
